ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: To study the photosynthetic characteristics of leaves in the upper and lower layers of the crown of a certain tree species, a student selected two types of leaves, A and B, from different layers of the crown and measured their net photosynthetic rates respectively. The results are shown in the figure. Answer the question according to the figure: From the figure, leaf A is a leaf from what position of the crown (fill in “upper layer” or “lower layer”)?

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: To study the photosynthetic characteristics of leaves in the upper and lower layers of the crown of a certain tree species, a student selected two types of leaves, A and B, from different layers of the crown and measured their net photosynthetic rates respectively. The results are shown in the figure. Answer the question according to the figure: From the figure, leaf A is a leaf from what position of the crown (fill in “upper layer” or “lower layer”)?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure, the horizontal axis is light intensity, and the vertical axis is net photosynthetic rate. The curve for leaf A rises relatively early as light intensity increases and approaches saturation, its maximum net photosynthetic rate is relatively low, and it still shows a downward trend after reaching a peak under relatively strong light; the curve for leaf B continues to rise under higher light intensity, and its maximum net photosynthetic rate is obviously higher than that of A. Then reason: Leaves in the lower layer of a crown are long in a weak-light environment, and usually have a lower light saturation point and a lower maximum net photosynthetic rate; leaves in the upper layer of a crown are adapted to strong light and have a higher light saturation point and maximum net photosynthetic rate. Therefore, leaf A conforms to the characteristics of leaves in the lower layer of the crown.
